rule.text: A break a review states (an interruption object with a value, beginning by the review) is recorded in the completed-work record (INTERRUPTION_DECLARED) whatever that review decides, the early clinical and eligibility routes included; a review refused as invalid input before it is read (contract, clock, week, list shape, carried state or model integrity) records nothing. The break stays in force until a return (REESTABLISH) is decided at or after it, or a newer declaration replaces it. A later review that states no break reads it as if it stated it: a weekly review or a return report applies it by the existing return recipe; another event kind is asked and applies nothing; a clinical route still comes first; a break whose own reason is clinical routes to a human again (F08 unchanged). The event that carried it is never applied with it.

openDefect.text: A newer stated break for a different, disjoint period ends the retention of a kept, unapplied one: the kept break's declared days leave the factual state and the re-entry is classed by the newer stop alone (a 14-day holiday kept, then a 7-day trip: SHORT, EASY 45/34, LONG 65, then THRESHOLD 41, where the 21-day stop declared at once gives MODERATE, EASY 15, LONG 20). UNREPORTED_TRAINING and the D18 ceiling do not protect against this under-classification. P17 counts the newer declaration as resolution and P08 passes, so no automated property detects it; a holdout case with two disjoint declared stops before an eligible review exercises it and is domain-judged without envelope. Same as R7D-FREEZE-1 when the newer break is stated in a weekly review; better than it otherwise. It conflicts with Founder D2 ("in every case the fact survives"); whether its correction is required before Phase 4 is the Founder's decision. Options left open by the SSCTR: ask whether the newer break corrects the kept one or is a separate stop (the existing episode question, I9), or read contiguous declared stops with no training between as one stop (against I9 as written).

f08.text: A break whose own reason is clinical is kept and, after qualified clearance, routes to a human at every later decision, also while the athlete trains and reports normally; no truthful conforming input leaves it. Only a newer, different declaration replaces it, and that exit is not uniformly conservative (a later nonclinical trip replaces an injury break and resumes SHORT with threshold work; relabelling the same dates as nonclinical gives MODERATE). Fails closed (no dose). Owners: Founder and PCG with the G04 owners, and the SSCTR; trigger: before any consumer use of the kept-break rule or any V1 authority claim.

ssctrFindings.finding: Days held after a kept break's stated end date are neither break nor asked. The re-entry is classed by the stated break alone, so a SHORT break held across a clinical route or a long silence resumes the last completed doses after a possibly longer real stop.

engineeringFindings.origin: new: consequence of D1-D3 with F08 open (disclosed in PREREG-3 residuals and INTERFACE-3)
engineeringFindings.finding: A break whose own reason is clinical is an absorbing state. After qualified clearance every later decision of every kind stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED for the rest of the program, whatever training is reported. No truthful conforming input leaves it: a return report with no break, the same break with nonclinical:true and clinicalReason:false, RECOVERED and weekly reviews all stay CLINICAL. Only a newer, different nonclinical declaration leaves it. A partial one (only episodeId) also replaces it, then asks. Fails closed (no dose); not a blocker; must be decided before any consumer use of the kept-break rule.

engineeringFindings.finding: INTERFACE-3 section 1 ('a refusal (HOLD)') and PREREG-3 Delta 1 ('sobrevive a ASK, HOLD e CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED') promise retention through HOLD. The runtime deliberately records nothing on integrity and contract refusals: the next plain review is VALID with no return. P17 has no carve-out, so such a case would score a SAFETY_BLOCKER. The R7D-CASE-1 client and checker cannot produce these reviews (they build the contract and lists, and reject unknown kinds), so no holdout case is expected to show it. Malformed execution facts do not refuse. The freeze record's rule text has the same omission.
